미군 B-26 조종사의 비행복·비행모·부양 장비. 의상 참고용이며 실제 성인 얼굴을 구성.
B-26 조종석의 나란한 좌석·아날로그 계기·투하 장치·캐노피 구조.
미군 마크 13 항공 어뢰의 긴 몸체·머리·꼬리·장착 구조. 폭탄으로 바꾸지 않는다.
아카기의 선체·선수 일장기·좌현 함교·우현 외향 하향 굴뚝. 좌우 구조를 바꾸지 않는다.
일본 연장 대공기관포의 평행한 두 포신·포가·조준기. 여러 그림은 실제 포 한 문을 설명한다.
일본 포수 복장·군모·급탄 장구. 포수와 보조 승무원이 실제로 사격하고 급탄한다.

shots.frame: 조종사 오른손과 투하 스위치 인서트에서 얼굴로. 앞 유리 너머 아카기.

beats.ko: 장갑 낀 엄지가 빨간 덮개를 튕겨 연다.
beats.en: a gloved thumb flips the red guard open

beats.ko: 조종사가 외친다.
beats.en: the PILOT shouts

beats.ko: 엄지가 스위치를 한 번 누르고, 기체가 가벼워지며 위로 살짝 뜬다.
beats.en: the thumb presses once; the aircraft, suddenly lighter, lifts slightly

shots.camera: 인서트 100mm 매크로 → 65mm 얼굴로 컷 없이 패닝.
shots.light: 계기판 그늘, 앞 유리의 강한 빛.
shots.sound: 스위치 딸깍, 짧은 외침, 투하 쇳소리.
shots.last_frame: 살짝 뜨는 기체에 몸이 눌리는 조종사.
shots.speaker: B-26 조종사

shots.frame: B-26 배 아래 측면. 전경: 해면. 중경: B-26 배와 어뢰. 배경: 수백 미터 앞 아카기 선체가 화면 오른쪽 절반을 채운다.

beats.ko: 어뢰가 거치대에서 분리되어 기수를 살짝 숙인 채 떨어진다.
beats.en: the torpedo separates from the rack and falls, nose slightly down

beats.ko: 얕게 물을 때리며 흰 물보라를 튀기고 사라진다.
beats.en: it slaps into the water shallow, throws white spray, and disappears

beats.ko: B-26은 빈 거치대를 보이며 계속 왼쪽으로 가고, 수면 아래로 곧은 기포 항적이 아카기 쪽으로 뻗는다.
beats.en: the B-26 continues left showing the empty rack; a straight bubble wake runs under the surface toward Akagi

shots.camera: 해면 위 2m 측면 추적 후 항적에 머문다.
shots.sound: 어뢰 이탈음, 물 때리는 소리, 엔진.
shots.direction: B-26 우→좌 / 어뢰 항적 아카기 방향.

shots.frame: 아카기 비행갑판 위, 섬 근처 높은 위치. 전경: 섬 옆 대공포좌 난간. 중경: 비행갑판(나무 결, 대기 중인 기체). 오른쪽에서 B-26이 갑판 위를 낮게 가로지른다.

beats.ko: B-26이 기수를 들어 비행갑판 바로 위를 스친다. 갑판 승무원들이 바닥에 엎드린다.
beats.en: the B-26 pulls up and skims just over the flight deck; deck crew throw themselves flat

beats.ko: 섬 옆 포좌의 포신들이 B-26을 따라 돌며 거의 자기 갑판을 향해 쏜다.
beats.en: barrels in the island tub swing after it, firing almost across their own deck

beats.ko: B-26이 반대편 바다로 빠져나가고 프로펠러 바람에 갑판 깃발이 찢어질 듯 펄럭인다.
beats.en: the B-26 clears the far side; its propwash whips the deck flags

shots.camera: 35mm, 섬 위에서 B-26을 따라 빠른 팬.
shots.sound: 머리 위를 찢는 쌍발 엔진, 대공포, 고함.

shots.frame: 아카기 선체 외경, 수면 높이. 화면 오른쪽: 선체와 섬. 오른쪽 위에서 왼쪽 아래로: 불붙은 두 번째 B-26.

beats.ko: 두 번째 B-26이 왼쪽 날개 뿌리에서 불길을 끌며 섬 높이로 날아든다.
beats.en: a second B-26 comes in at island height trailing fire from its left wing root

beats.ko: 섬 옆을 몇 미터 차이로 스치고 승무원들이 몸을 숙인다.
beats.en: it misses the island by metres; crewmen duck

beats.ko: 선체 너머 바다에 처박혀 거대한 불기둥과 물기둥이 솟는다.
beats.en: it slams into the sea beyond the hull; a huge column of fire and water rises

shots.camera: 수면 위 낮은 위치, 기체를 따라 팬 후 충돌에서 고정.
shots.light: 주황 화염과 검은 연기, 회청색 선체.
shots.fx: 불은 날개 뿌리에서만, 연기는 바람 따라 오른쪽.
shots.sound: 불타는 엔진의 절규, 충돌 폭음, 물 쏟아지는 소리.

shots.frame: 아카기 측면 포좌 클로즈업. 사수와 급탄수, 뒤로 연기 낀 하늘.

beats.ko: 사수가 소리 지르며 남은 기체를 쫓아 포를 돌린다.
beats.en: the gunner yells, swinging the mount after the remaining aircraft

beats.ko: 급탄수가 새 탄창을 내리꽂고 뜨거운 탄피에 손을 데어 움찔한다.
beats.en: the loader slams a fresh magazine, flinching as hot brass burns his hand

beats.ko: 탄피 더미가 발목까지 쌓인다.
beats.en: brass piles up to their ankles

shots.camera: 40mm 핸드헬드, 반동에 흔들림.
shots.sound: 연사, 단어 없는 고함, 탄피.

shots.frame: 높은 사선. 전경 아래: 곧은 기포 항적. 배경: 아카기 선체.

beats.ko: 어뢰 항적이 아카기 옆구리를 향해 곧게 달린다.
beats.en: the torpedo wake runs straight at Akagi's side

beats.ko: 아카기 함수가 하얗게 물을 가르며 막 돌기 시작한다.
beats.en: Akagi's bow throws white water as she just begins to turn

shots.camera: 높은 사선에서 항적을 따라 느린 푸시.
shots.light: 반짝이는 해면 위 흰 기포 선.
shots.sound: 물살, 먼 포성, 아카기 기관의 진동.

B-26 CO-PILOT — American, 25. Round face, black hair, thick joined eyebrows, dark-brown eyes, soft rounded chin, headset over his flight helmet.
JAPANESE AA GUNNER — Japanese sailor, 21. Thin face, sharp jaw, shaved head under a steel helmet with chin strap, gritted teeth, white undershirt, sweat; sits in the pointer seat of a twin 25mm mount.

Americans: varied European-American ancestry (Irish, Italian, German, Polish), varied hair colour, deeper-set eyes, higher nose bridges, forearm hair, sunburnt red-pink skin, stubble, sweat. Real 1942 faces — no movie-star polish.
Japanese: authentic adult Japanese men of 1942 — lean, wiry, compact builds; enlisted heads shaved or near-shaved, officers short-cropped; monolid or hooded eyes, straight lower nose bridge, defined cheekbones, bronze tan, clean-shaven unless stated. Every other extra has a clearly different face; no clones.

[DIRECTION & PHYSICS]
American flight paths, ship headings, muzzles and profiles read RIGHT-TO-LEFT; Japanese read LEFT-TO-RIGHT — by camera placement, never by mirroring.
Propellers are blurred discs; aircraft keep exact shape; torpedoes fall nose-slightly-down, splash, then run straight leaving a bubble wake; bombs keep forward momentum; recoil, casings, spray and debris obey gravity. A destroyed aircraft never reappears. The camera never passes through glass, walls or hulls.

[NEGATIVE]
No on-screen text, subtitles, timestamps, logos, watermarks, letterbox. No music, no narration. No modern objects. No anime/CG/plastic look, no waxy skin, no cloned faces, no extra fingers or limbs.
Exactly one torpedo leaves the hero B-26 and the rack stays empty afterwards. The torpedo drops close beside the carrier, not far away. Akagi's island is on her PORT side. No hit on Akagi in this clip.

[STRUCTURE]
28s, 6 shots, hard cuts. Timings are clip time.
First frame: B-26 cockpit: the PILOT's thumb over the red release switch; Akagi's hull fills the windscreen.

[SHOTS]
Shot 1 (0–4s) — RELEASE
Refs: @image3, @image4
Frame: Insert of the PILOT's right hand on the release switch, then his face; Akagi beyond the windscreen.
Action:
- 0–1s: a gloved thumb flips the red guard open
- 1–2.5s: the PILOT shouts
- 2.5–4s: the thumb presses once; the aircraft, suddenly lighter, lifts slightly
Dialogue (B-26 PILOT, English, barked) at 1–2.5s: "Release!"
Camera: 100mm macro insert, then a whip pan to his face at 65mm.
Light: panel shadow, hard light through the windscreen.
Sound: switch click, the shout, the clank of release.
Ends on: the PILOT pressed into his seat as the aircraft lifts.

Shot 2 (4–9s) · CUT TO — DROP — beside the carrier
Refs: @image2, @image5, @image1, @image6
Frame: Low side view under the B-26. Foreground: the sea surface. Midground: the belly and the torpedo (@image5). Background: Akagi's hull, a few hundred metres off, filling the right half.
Action:
- 4–5.5s: the torpedo separates from the rack and falls, nose slightly down
- 5.5–7s: it slaps into the water shallow, throws white spray, and disappears
- 7–9s: the B-26 continues left showing the empty rack; a straight bubble wake runs under the surface toward Akagi
Camera: side tracking 2 metres above the water, then hold on the wake.
Light: sea glare, white spray.
Sound: release clank, the slap of water, engines.
Ends on: the empty rack and the running wake.

Shot 3 (9–14s) · CUT TO — OVER THE DECK
Refs: @image2, @image6, @image7
Frame: High beside Akagi's island. Foreground: an AA tub rail by the island. Midground: the flight deck — wood planking, parked aircraft. A B-26 crosses low over the deck from the right.
Action:
- 9–11s: the B-26 pulls up and skims just over the flight deck; deck crew throw themselves flat
- 11–12.5s: barrels in the island tub swing after it, firing almost across their own deck
- 12.5–14s: the B-26 clears the far side; its propwash whips the deck flags
Camera: 35mm from the island, fast pan with the B-26.
Light: hard deck glare, drifting smoke shadows.
Sound: twin engines tearing overhead, AA, shouts.
Ends on: the B-26's tail escaping.

Shot 4 (14–19s) · CUT TO — THE BURNING ONE
Refs: @image2, @image6, @image1
Frame: Akagi's hull from sea level. Frame right: hull and island. From upper right to lower left: a second B-26, on fire.
Action:
- 14–15.5s: a second B-26 comes in at island height trailing fire from its left wing root
- 15.5–17s: it misses the island by metres; crewmen duck
- 17–19s: it slams into the sea beyond the hull; a huge column of fire and water rises

Light: orange fire and black smoke against the blue-grey hull.

Sound: the screaming burning engine, the impact, water crashing down.
Ends on: the column collapsing beside the hull.

Shot 5 (19–23s) · CUT TO — NO PAUSE — Japanese gunners
Refs: @image7, @image8
Frame: Close on an AA mount on Akagi's side: the AA GUNNER and AA LOADER, smoky sky behind.
Action:
- 19–20.5s: the gunner yells, swinging the mount after the remaining aircraft
- 20.5–22s: the loader slams a fresh magazine, flinching as hot brass burns his hand
- 22–23s: brass piles up to their ankles

Light: muzzle flash, smoke-dimmed sun.
Sound: bursts, wordless yelling, brass.
Ends on: the gun never stops.

Shot 6 (23–28s) · CUT TO — THE WAKE RUNS
Refs: @image1, @image5, @image6
Frame: High oblique. Foreground: the straight bubble wake. Background: Akagi's hull.
Action:
- 23–25.5s: the torpedo wake runs straight at Akagi's side
- 25.5–28s: Akagi's bow throws white water as she just begins to turn

Light: white bubble line on the glittering sea.

Ends on: the wake and the turning bow.

clips.prompt:
[STYLE LOCK]
Photoreal live-action WWII epic, Battle of Midway, June 4 1942. Large-format cinema camera, spherical primes, fine film grain, soft highlight roll-off, deep atmospheric haze at distance.
Palette: steel-teal sea, milky high-key sky with towering cumulus, white coral sand, olive-drab, khaki and dark navy, warm tanned skin. Orange fire only at the instant of an explosion or a burning wing; flak is black, smoke charcoal, sea spray white. No oversaturated cyan, no game sheen.
Every frame in three layers: dark foreground occluder (sandbag, barrel, window frame, wing edge, hull rail) — subject — vast sky, sea or battle beyond. Exteriors: men small against the sky. Interiors: hard window light, haze, and the battle outside always visible or audible.
Real-time speed, no slow motion. 16:9, 1080p. Light, haze, smoke and wind stay continuous across cuts.

[TIME & PLACE]
Late morning: high sun, gunsmoke haze drifting across the fleet.

[IMAGES — all references, none as start/end frame]
@image1 [BG] open Pacific surface, far horizon, broken cumulus
@image2 [ASSET] Kagero-class destroyer: hull, two funnels, gun mounts
@image3 [ASSET] US Mark 13 aerial torpedo: long body, nose, tail, mount
@image4 [ASSET] carrier Akagi: hull, hinomaru on bow, island on PORT side, downward-curved funnel on STARBOARD side
@image5 [ASSET] Japanese twin 25mm AA mount: two parallel barrels, carriage, sights
@image6 [ASSET] Japanese AA crew uniform, helmet, magazine gear
@image7 [BG] Akagi bridge interior: narrow windows, chart table, pillars, passage

[REFERENCE LOCK]
BG images: copy layout, materials and geography only — not their camera, light or colour.
Aircraft/ship/weapon images: exact silhouette, structure, paint, markings, number of engines, barrels and funnels; never morph types.
Costume sheets: uniform and gear only, worn by living men with the CAST LOCK faces. Never show sheets, labels, mannequins or multiple views.
US insignia 1942: white star in blue circle, no red centre, no side bars. Japanese: red hinomaru.

[CAST LOCK — same faces in every shot]
JAPANESE AA GUNNER — Japanese sailor, 21. Thin face, sharp jaw, shaved head under a steel helmet with chin strap, gritted teeth, white undershirt, sweat; sits in the pointer seat of a twin 25mm mount.
JAPANESE AA LOADER — Japanese sailor, 19. Round boyish face, near-shaved head, wide-set eyes, flushed cheeks, white towel around his neck, slams 15-round box magazines onto the gun.
Americans: varied European-American ancestry (Irish, Italian, German, Polish), varied hair colour, deeper-set eyes, higher nose bridges, forearm hair, sunburnt red-pink skin, stubble, sweat. Real 1942 faces — no movie-star polish.
Japanese: authentic adult Japanese men of 1942 — lean, wiry, compact builds; enlisted heads shaved or near-shaved, officers short-cropped; monolid or hooded eyes, straight lower nose bridge, defined cheekbones, bronze tan, clean-shaven unless stated. Natural, dignified — never caricature, never modern idol styling.
Every other extra has a clearly different face; no clones.

[DIRECTION & PHYSICS]
American flight paths, ship headings, muzzles and profiles read RIGHT-TO-LEFT; Japanese read LEFT-TO-RIGHT — by camera placement, never by mirroring.
Propellers are blurred discs; aircraft keep exact shape; torpedoes fall nose-slightly-down, splash, then run straight leaving a bubble wake; bombs keep forward momentum; recoil, casings, spray and debris obey gravity. A destroyed aircraft never reappears. The camera never passes through glass, walls or hulls.

[NEGATIVE]
No on-screen text, subtitles, timestamps, logos, watermarks, letterbox. No music, no narration. No modern objects. No anime/CG/plastic look, no waxy skin, no cloned faces, no extra fingers or limbs.
NO aircraft crash in the destroyer shots — only the torpedo. The camera never passes through glass.

[STRUCTURE]
20s, 4 shots, hard cuts. Timings are clip time.
First frame: a destroyer's exterior: two funnels, gunsmoke over the mounts, hull filling the right half; a torpedo falls from the sky.

[SHOTS]
Shot 1 (0–5s) — SPLASH — beside the destroyer
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image3
Frame: Water level. Right half: the destroyer (@image2) — hull and two funnels. Upper left sky: a falling torpedo (@image3); its aircraft already out of frame.
Action:
- 0–1.5s: a torpedo falls from the sky, nose slightly down
- 1.5–3s: it enters the water 20 metres off the hull; a narrow white column rises
- 3–5s: spray sheets over the low rail; crew duck; the hull is untouched
Camera: low fixed shot above the water, a short shake at the splash.
Light: white column, grey hull.
Sound: the torpedo's falling whistle, the entry slap, spray.
Ends on: spray settling on the rail.

Shot 2 (5–10s) · CUT TO — RUNNING — and missing
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image3, @image6
Frame: On the destroyer's rail. Foreground: the rail and a crewman pointing. Below: a bubble wake running alongside the hull.
Action:
- 5–7s: crewmen at the rail point down at the wake, wordless shouts
- 7–9s: the destroyer swings her bow; the wake slides away from the hull
- 9–10s: the wake vanishes into open sea
Camera: 35mm handheld, from the rail looking down.
Light: glare off the wet deck.
Sound: shouts, machinery, rushing water.
Ends on: crew staring at empty sea.

Shot 3 (10–14s) · CUT TO — FIRE ON — the destroyer's guns
Refs: @image5, @image6, @image2
Frame: Medium on the destroyer's AA mount: AA GUNNER and AA LOADER; smoky sky and distant Akagi behind.
Action:
- 10–12s: the gunner swings skyward and fires
- 12–14s: the loader swaps magazines; brass rolls across the deck
Camera: 40mm low angle, recoil shake.
Light: muzzle flash, smoke, backlight.
Sound: bursts, brass.
Ends on: gunsmoke drifting toward Akagi's island.

Shot 4 (14–20s) · CUT TO — APPROACH — the bridge
Refs: @image4, @image5, @image7
Frame: Akagi's island at bridge-window height. Foreground: barrels of an island AA tub, soft. Midground: the bridge windows with silhouettes inside. Background: flak and crossing American aircraft.
Action:
- 14–16s: the camera moves past the firing tub toward the bridge windows
- 16–18s: through the glass, Nagumo's capped silhouette; an American aircraft crosses the sky right-to-left in front
- 18–20s: a window pillar fills the frame completely — cut on this wipe
Camera: crane-like move outside the island, wipe cut on the pillar.
Light: reflections on the bridge glass, dark interior.
Sound: tub fire, wind, rattling glass.
Ends on: the window pillar filling the frame.

[AUDIO]
Speak only the quoted lines, once each, in the stated language, at the stated moment. Diegetic sound only — wind, sea, engines, guns, metal, wordless voices — carried across cuts. No music, no narration.

clips.title: 아수라장 속 첫 명령
clips.beat: 함교 밖은 아수라장이다. 미군기가 창 앞을 가로지르고 함대의 포가 쉬지 않는다. 그 속에서 나구모는 미드웨이 2차 공격을 위한 육상 폭탄 교체를 명령한다.
clips.first_frame: 함교 내부, 창틀 기둥이 오른쪽으로 빠지며 열린다. 나구모의 등 너머 창 가득 대공 연기와 가로지르는 미군기.
clips.first_frame_en: Akagi bridge interior as a window pillar slides off to the right: beyond Nagumo's back, the windows are full of flak and a crossing American aircraft.
clips.state: 나구모 군모 항상. 창밖 전투가 모든 샷에서 보이거나 들린다(창·진동·막힌 포성). 대본의 '구축함 선실'은 아카기 함교로 각색.
clips.exit: 명령이 전달되고, 나구모는 창밖 불타는 미군기를 본다. 외부 포성이 다음 클립의 미 함대 부감 엔진음으로 넘어간다.
clips.time_of_day: Late morning, interior: hard white window light, gunsmoke haze inside the bridge, flashes from outside.

아카기의 선체·선수 일장기·좌현 함교·우현 외향 하향 굴뚝. 좌우 구조를 바꾸지 않는다.

일본 연장 대공기관포의 평행한 두 포신·포가·조준기. 여러 그림은 실제 포 한 문을 설명한다.

shots.frame: 함교 와이드. 전경: 해도대 모서리와 흔들리는 전성관. 중경: 해도대를 짚은 나구모(등, 군모), 오가는 장교들. 뒤 벽 전체가 창: B-26이 창 앞을 낮게 가로지르고, 대공 연기, 구축함의 포구 섬광, 근탄 물기둥.

beats.ko: B-26이 창 앞을 오른쪽→왼쪽으로 낮게 지나가며 창 전체가 떨린다.
beats.en: a B-26 passes low right-to-left; every pane rattles

beats.ko: 배가 기울며 장교 한 명이 비틀거리고 해도 위 컴퍼스가 미끄러진다.
beats.en: the ship heels; an officer staggers; dividers slide across the chart

beats.ko: 근탄 물기둥이 창을 덮었다 쏟아져 내린다. 나구모는 해도대를 짚은 채 움직이지 않는다.
beats.en: a near-miss column sheets over the glass and falls away; Nagumo, hands on the table, does not move

shots.camera: 24mm 와이드, 실내 깊은 곳에서 느린 푸시 인.
shots.light: 창의 강한 백라이트, 실내의 포연 헤이즈, 바깥 섬광이 실내를 깜빡인다.
shots.sound: 막힌 포성, 유리 떨림, 강철의 신음, 전성관 목소리(단어 없음).

shots.frame: 나구모 얼굴 클로즈업, 화면 왼쪽 3분의 1에서 오른쪽(창)을 본다. 군모 차양 그늘. 배경: 흐린 창과 섬광.

beats.ko: 창밖 폭발 섬광이 얼굴을 주황으로 한 번 칠한다. 그는 눈 하나 깜빡이지 않는다.
beats.en: an outside explosion washes his face orange once; he does not blink

beats.ko: 콧수염 아래 입술이 굳게 다물리고 턱 근육이 움직인다.
beats.en: his lips press tight under the mustache; a jaw muscle works

shots.camera: 85mm, 락 오프, 함선 진동만.
shots.sound: 폭음, 유리 떨림.

shots.frame: 투숏. 나구모 왼쪽, 참모 오른쪽(클립보드). 그 사이로 창: 포좌의 사격, 미군기.

beats.ko: 나구모가 창에서 몸을 돌려 참모를 본다.
beats.en: Nagumo turns from the window to the staff officer

beats.ko: 단호하게 명령한다.
beats.en: he gives the order, firm

beats.ko: 참모가 받아 적으며 고개를 끄덕인다. 창 뒤로 대공 연기가 또 핀다.
beats.en: the officer writes and nods; another flak burst blooms behind the glass

shots.camera: 50mm, 두 사람 사이로 아주 느린 달리 인.
shots.sound: 명령, 막힌 포성, 연필 소리.
shots.dialogue: ミッドウェーへ第二次攻撃準備！陸用爆弾に換装せよ！
shots.speaker: 나구모
shots.meaning: 미드웨이로 2차 공격 준비! 육상 폭탄으로 교체하라!

shots.frame: 참모 클로즈업, 오른쪽 3분의 1. 안경에 창빛.

beats.ko: 참모가 짧게 답한다.
beats.en: he answers, short

beats.ko: 즉시 몸을 돌려 오른쪽 통신 위치로 걷는다.
beats.en: he turns at once toward the signal station

shots.camera: 65mm, 그가 돌 때 짧은 팬.
shots.sound: 짧은 대답, 구두 소리.
shots.speaker: 일본 참모

shots.frame: 통신 위치. 전경: 무전기 다이얼(@image9). 중경: 수화기를 든 통신병과 쪽지를 건네는 참모. 배경: 작은 창, 바깥 물보라.

beats.ko: 참모가 쪽지를 건네고 통신병이 수화기에 대고 빠르게 전달한다(입 모양만, 대사 없음).
beats.en: the officer hands over the slip; the signalman relays it rapidly into the handset — mouth moving, no audible line

beats.ko: 근탄 물보라가 작은 창을 덮어 실내가 순간 어두워진다.
beats.en: near-miss spray covers the small window; the room darkens for a moment

beats.ko: 물이 흘러내리며 빛이 돌아오고, 통신병이 다이얼을 돌린다.
beats.en: water streams off, light returns; the signalman turns a dial

shots.camera: 50mm, 무전기 옆 낮은 위치.
shots.sound: 무전 잡음, 빠른 중얼거림, 창을 때리는 물.

shots.frame: 나구모 어깨 너머로 창. 창 너머 멀리: 불붙은 미군기가 연기를 끌며 바다로 떨어진다. 함대의 포연.

beats.ko: 불붙은 기체가 연기 줄을 끌며 바다에 떨어진다.
beats.en: the burning aircraft falls, trailing smoke into the sea

beats.ko: 나구모가 짧게 숨을 내쉰다.
beats.en: Nagumo exhales, short

beats.ko: 흰 장갑 낀 주먹이 해도 위에 놓인다.
beats.en: his white-gloved fist settles on the chart

shots.camera: 65mm 어깨 너머, 락 오프.
shots.sound: 멀리 낙수음, 이어지는 포성.

Light: window backlight, side light on faces.

clips.prompt:
[STYLE LOCK]
Photoreal live-action WWII epic, Battle of Midway, June 4 1942. Large-format cinema camera, spherical primes, fine film grain, soft highlight roll-off, deep atmospheric haze at distance.
Palette: steel-teal sea, milky high-key sky with towering cumulus, white coral sand, olive-drab, khaki and dark navy, warm tanned skin. Orange fire only at the instant of an explosion or a burning wing; flak is black, smoke charcoal, sea spray white. No oversaturated cyan, no game sheen.
Every frame in three layers: dark foreground occluder (sandbag, barrel, window frame, wing edge, hull rail) — subject — vast sky, sea or battle beyond. Exteriors: men small against the sky. Interiors: hard window light, haze, and the battle outside always visible or audible.
Real-time speed, no slow motion. 16:9, 1080p. Light, haze, smoke and wind stay continuous across cuts.

[TIME & PLACE]
Late morning, US carrier: bright open sky, clean sea, wind over the deck, no smoke.

[IMAGES — all references, none as start/end frame]
@image1 [BG] open Pacific surface, far horizon, broken cumulus
@image2 [ASSET] USS Enterprise CV-6 1942: straight flight deck, STARBOARD island, hull
@image3 [BG] Enterprise wooden flight deck, deck edge, launch lane
@image4 [ASSET] F4F-4 Wildcat on deck, wings spread, wheels down
@image5 [ASSET] F4F-4 Wildcat in flight, main wheels retracted
@image6 [ASSET] TBD-1 Devastator: long tandem canopy, blue-grey, corrugated wings, main wheels half-protruding when retracted
@image7 [ASSET] US flight-deck crew clothing, cloth helmet, signal role
@image8 [ASSET] US Navy aircrew flight suit, helmet, yellow life vest

[REFERENCE LOCK]
BG images: copy layout, materials and geography only — not their camera, light or colour.
Aircraft/ship/weapon images: exact silhouette, structure, paint, markings, number of engines, barrels and funnels; never morph types.
Costume sheets: uniform and gear only, worn by living men with the CAST LOCK faces. Never show sheets, labels, mannequins or multiple views.
US insignia 1942: white star in blue circle, no red centre, no side bars. Japanese: red hinomaru.

[CAST LOCK — same faces in every shot]
FLIGHT DECK OFFICER — American Navy, 34. Lean leathery face, squinting pale eyes, sharp nose, yellow jersey and cloth helmet, a chequered flag in his right hand.
Americans: varied European-American ancestry (Irish, Italian, German, Polish), varied hair colour, deeper-set eyes, higher nose bridges, forearm hair, sunburnt red-pink skin, stubble, sweat. Real 1942 faces — no movie-star polish.
Every other extra has a clearly different face; no clones.

[DIRECTION & PHYSICS]
American flight paths, ship headings, muzzles and profiles read RIGHT-TO-LEFT; Japanese read LEFT-TO-RIGHT — by camera placement, never by mirroring.
Propellers are blurred discs; aircraft keep exact shape; torpedoes fall nose-slightly-down, splash, then run straight leaving a bubble wake; bombs keep forward momentum; recoil, casings, spray and debris obey gravity. A destroyed aircraft never reappears. The camera never passes through glass, walls or hulls.

[NEGATIVE]
No on-screen text, subtitles, timestamps, logos, watermarks, letterbox. No music, no narration. No modern objects. No anime/CG/plastic look, no waxy skin, no cloned faces, no extra fingers or limbs.
Show the carrier and multiple airborne aircraft together — the origin must be obvious. No repeated single-aircraft preparation inserts. Enterprise's island stays on her STARBOARD side.

[STRUCTURE]
26s, 5 shots, hard cuts. Timings are clip time.
First frame: low over the sea off Enterprise's bow: beyond the bow two aircraft already climb away to the left, a third just leaving the deck edge.

[SHOTS]
Shot 1 (0–5s) — LAUNCH — carrier and aircraft in one frame
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image5, @image6
Frame: Low over the water, front three-quarter off the bow. Right: Enterprise's (@image2) bow and deck edge. Left sky: two aircraft already up. Deck edge: a third lifting off. Behind it: more aircraft with props turning.
Action:
- 0–2s: the third aircraft dips off the deck edge, then climbs
- 2–3.5s: the two ahead bank left and climb
- 3.5–5s: the next aircraft rolls up to the launch spot
Camera: 24mm, 2 metres above the water, slow tracking toward the bow.
Light: bright sky, bow spray, clean sea.
Sound: bow wave, many engines, deck wind.
Ends on: three in the sky, the next on deck.

Shot 2 (5–10s) · CUT TO — THE FLAG
Refs: @image3, @image4, @image7
Frame: Deck level. Foreground right: the FLIGHT DECK OFFICER with a chequered flag. Midground: an F4F (@image4) at full power, brakes on, tail bucking. Background: crew crouched at the deck edge, waiting aircraft.
Action:
- 5–7s: the officer whirls the flag fast over his head; the engine screams to full power
- 7–8s: he snaps the flag down and forward, crouching
- 8–10s: the F4F releases and races down the deck right-to-left; propwash whips the officer's jersey
Acting: the officer is expressionless, in rhythm — he has done this a thousand times.
Camera: 35mm low on the deck, pan with the aircraft after release.
Light: hard sun, yellow jersey, glinting propeller disc.
Sound: full-power engine, wind, deck vibration.
Ends on: the F4F racing for the deck end.

Shot 3 (10–14s) · CUT TO — OFF THE BOW
Refs: @image4, @image5, @image1
Frame: Catwalk beside the deck end. Foreground: catwalk rail. Midground: the F4F leaving the deck. Background: sea.
Action:
- 10–11.5s: the F4F leaves the deck and sags once
- 11.5–13s: it retracts its wheels and climbs
- 13–14s: spray wets the catwalk
Camera: 50mm from the catwalk, tilt up with the climb.
Light: backlight, sparkling spray.
Sound: engine Doppler, spray.
Ends on: the climbing F4F in silhouette.

Shot 4 (14–19s) · CUT TO — THE HEAVY ONES — torpedo bombers
Refs: @image3, @image6, @image8
Frame: From behind on the deck: a TBD (@image6) with a torpedo under its belly lumbers down the deck; pilot and rear gunner in the canopy, no face detail.
Action:
- 14–16s: the TBD accelerates heavily; its tail lifts
- 16–18s: it barely lifts at the deck end, the torpedo just clearing the waves
- 18–19s: behind it the next TBD takes the launch spot
Camera: 75mm compressed from high behind on the deck.
Light: heat shimmer, hard sun.
Sound: heavy engine, deck wind.
Ends on: the TBD just above the sea.

Shot 5 (19–26s) · CUT TO — STRIKE GROUP — heading for Japan
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image5, @image6
Frame: High aerial. Foreground: a near F4F wing. Midground: a low line of TBDs with F4Fs above. Lower right behind: Enterprise shrinking, her wake. Left: the horizon — toward the Japanese.
Action:
- 19–21.5s: the strike group forms up above the carrier
- 21.5–24s: the formation settles on a heading right-to-left toward the horizon
- 24–26s: the near wing slices past, revealing a larger formation behind
Camera: aerial tracking, ending on a wing wipe.
Light: high sun, cloud shadows.
Sound: a chorus of engines, wind.
Ends on: the strike group heading for the horizon.

[AUDIO]
Speak only the quoted lines, once each, in the stated language, at the stated moment. Diegetic sound only — wind, sea, engines, guns, metal, wordless voices — carried across cuts. No music, no narration.

clips.prompt:
[STYLE LOCK]
Photoreal live-action WWII epic, Battle of Midway, June 4 1942. Large-format cinema camera, spherical primes, fine film grain, soft highlight roll-off, deep atmospheric haze at distance.
Palette: steel-teal sea, milky high-key sky with towering cumulus, white coral sand, olive-drab, khaki and dark navy, warm tanned skin. Orange fire only at the instant of an explosion or a burning wing; flak is black, smoke charcoal, sea spray white. No oversaturated cyan, no game sheen.
Every frame in three layers: dark foreground occluder (sandbag, barrel, window frame, wing edge, hull rail) — subject — vast sky, sea or battle beyond. Exteriors: men small against the sky. Interiors: hard window light, haze, and the battle outside always visible or audible.
Real-time speed, no slow motion. 16:9, 1080p. Light, haze, smoke and wind stay continuous across cuts.

[TIME & PLACE]
Late morning, interior: hard window light, gunsmoke haze, flashes outside.

[IMAGES — all references, none as start/end frame]
@image1 [BG] Akagi bridge interior: narrow windows, chart table, pillars, passage
@image2 [ASSET] Nagumo approved face, age, mustache, dark uniform, peaked cap
@image3 [ASSET] Japanese staff officer uniform and cap
@image4 [ASSET] Japanese fixed radio set, dials, corded handset
@image5 [BG] open Pacific surface, far horizon, broken cumulus
@image6 [ASSET] Japanese twin 25mm AA mount: two parallel barrels, carriage, sights
@image7 [ASSET] Japanese AA crew uniform, helmet, magazine gear
@image8 [ASSET] early B-26 Marauder twin-engine bomber, olive drab, short wings, wheels retracted in flight
@image9 [ASSET] A6M2 Zero, grey-green, red hinomaru, wheels retracted, no drop tank

[REFERENCE LOCK]
BG images: copy layout, materials and geography only — not their camera, light or colour.
Aircraft/ship/weapon images: exact silhouette, structure, paint, markings, number of engines, barrels and funnels; never morph types.
Costume sheets: uniform and gear only, worn by living men with the CAST LOCK faces. Never show sheets, labels, mannequins or multiple views.
US insignia 1942: white star in blue circle, no red centre, no side bars. Japanese: red hinomaru.

[CAST LOCK — same faces in every shot]
NAGUMO — Japanese vice admiral, 55 (approved reference image governs). Broad heavy face, deep nasolabial folds, heavy-lidded drooping eyes, short grey toothbrush mustache, grey close-cropped sideburns. Peaked naval cap in EVERY shot. Dark navy uniform, white gloves.
STAFF OFFICER — Japanese officer, 42. Slim oval face, narrow chin, thin metal-rimmed rectangular glasses, clean-shaven, neat hair under his cap, composed but tight mouth, clipboard of message forms.
SIGNALMAN — Japanese sailor, 22. Thin boyish face, round cheeks, near-shaved head, headset clamped over a cloth cap, pencil behind his ear.
Japanese: authentic adult Japanese men of 1942 — lean, wiry, compact builds; enlisted heads shaved or near-shaved, officers short-cropped; monolid or hooded eyes, straight lower nose bridge, defined cheekbones, bronze tan, clean-shaven unless stated. Natural, dignified — never caricature, never modern idol styling.
Every other extra has a clearly different face; no clones.

[DIRECTION & PHYSICS]
American flight paths, ship headings, muzzles and profiles read RIGHT-TO-LEFT; Japanese read LEFT-TO-RIGHT — by camera placement, never by mirroring.
Propellers are blurred discs; aircraft keep exact shape; torpedoes fall nose-slightly-down, splash, then run straight leaving a bubble wake; bombs keep forward momentum; recoil, casings, spray and debris obey gravity. A destroyed aircraft never reappears. The camera never passes through glass, walls or hulls.

[NEGATIVE]
No on-screen text, subtitles, timestamps, logos, watermarks, letterbox. No music, no narration. No modern objects. No anime/CG/plastic look, no waxy skin, no cloned faces, no extra fingers or limbs.
Outside the windows is NEVER calm. Nagumo always wears his cap. The order is torpedoes and armour-piercing bombs.

[STRUCTURE]
30s, 6 shots, hard cuts. Timings are clip time.
First frame: Akagi bridge: NAGUMO paces two steps between the window and the chart table, clenching and opening his white gloves; flak and an American aircraft outside.

[SHOTS]
Shot 1 (0–5s) — RESTLESS
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image3, @image8
Frame: Bridge medium-wide: NAGUMO pacing between window and table; STAFF OFFICER behind left, SIGNALMAN right; windows: an American aircraft passing, flak.
Action:
- 0–2s: Nagumo takes two steps to the window, stops, turns back
- 2–3.5s: he clenches and opens a white-gloved hand
- 3.5–5s: an American aircraft passes low outside; every head turns to the window
Acting: the body of a man who cannot decide; his eyes keep returning to the two papers.
Camera: 35mm, short pans back and forth with his pacing.
Light: window backlight, flickering flashes.
Sound: shoes on steel, muffled guns, an aircraft passing.
Ends on: all eyes on the window.

Shot 2 (5–9s) · CUT TO — JOLT
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image5
Frame: Close on the chart table: the two papers, NAGUMO's hand above them.
Action:
- 5–6.5s: a near miss jolts the bridge; dust sifts from the ceiling
- 6.5–8s: Nagumo grips the table edge and holds
- 8–9s: dust settles on the papers; his eyes stop on the new report
Camera: 50mm, high angle tilting up to his face.
Light: window light through falling dust.
Sound: a dull blast, groaning steel, sifting dust.
Ends on: his eyes decided.

Shot 3 (9–16s) · CUT TO — DECISION
Refs: @image2, @image3, @image1, @image6
Frame: NAGUMO in front three-quarter medium close-up, the STAFF OFFICER on the right edge; behind, a firing AA tub through the window.
Action:
- 9–10.5s: he sweeps the Midway attack order aside with the back of his hand
- 10.5–11.5s: he slaps the new report flat with his palm
- 11.5–16s: he gives the order, resolved
Dialogue (NAGUMO, Japanese, resolved, rising) at 11.5–16s: "ミッドウェー攻撃隊を、魚雷と徹甲爆弾に再換装せよ！敵艦隊を撃滅する！"
Camera: 65mm, slow push-in.
Light: window side light, deep-set shadowed eyes.
Sound: paper sliding, the palm slap, the order, muffled guns.
Ends on: his mouth set hard.

Shot 4 (16–21s) · CUT TO — THE RISK
Refs: @image3, @image1
Frame: STAFF OFFICER close-up, right third; glasses, pencil stopped.
Action:
- 16–17.5s: his pencil stops mid-word
- 17.5–20s: he voices the risk, carefully
- 20–21s: a blast flashes in his lenses
Dialogue (STAFF OFFICER, Japanese, careful, hesitant) at 17.5–20s: "換装中に攻撃されたら……。"
Camera: 85mm, locked-off.
Light: the window reflected in his glasses.
Sound: hesitant voice, a blast.
Ends on: the officer looking at Nagumo.

Shot 5 (21–25s) · CUT TO — FIGHTERS — there!
Refs: @image2, @image1, @image9
Frame: NAGUMO and the window: he points; beyond the glass, two Zeros (@image9) pass left-to-right.
Action:
- 21–22.5s: Nagumo thrusts an arm toward the window
- 22.5–25s: he snaps it out; two Zeros sweep past beyond the glass
Acting: his voice is strong but his jaw never relaxes.
Dialogue (NAGUMO, Japanese, forceful, cutting off) at 22.5–25s: "戦闘機がいるだろう！"
Camera: 50mm, short pan along his arm to the window.
Light: silhouette against the window.
Sound: the shout, Zero engines.
Ends on: the pointing arm held; tension in his jaw.

Shot 6 (25–30s) · CUT TO — EXECUTE
Refs: @image3, @image4, @image1
Frame: The STAFF OFFICER walks to the signal station; NAGUMO stays at the table; the officer's shoulder passes close to camera.
Action:
- 25–27s: the officer gives a short bow and heads for the signal station
- 27–28.5s: the signalman lifts the handset and takes it down
- 28.5–30s: the officer's shoulder fills the lens completely — cut
Camera: 35mm, following the officer, ending on a shoulder wipe.
Light: window light, dial lamps.
Sound: footsteps, radio static.
Ends on: the frame blacked by the shoulder.

[AUDIO]
Speak only the quoted lines, once each, in the stated language, at the stated moment. Diegetic sound only — wind, sea, engines, guns, metal, wordless voices — carried across cuts. No music, no narration.

clips.first_frame: 격납고 와이드. 날개를 맞댄 B5N 줄, 배 아래 육상 폭탄. 낮은 강철 천장, 흔들리는 작업등, 열기의 아지랑이. 무장 반장이 호루라기를 문다.
clips.first_frame_en: hangar wide: rows of B5N2s wingtip to wingtip, land bombs under their bellies; low steel ceiling, swinging work lamps, heat haze; the ORDNANCE CHIEF puts a whistle to his lips.

clips.entry: C10의 어깨 와이프에서 이어진다(보고 장면 없음).
clips.exit: 격납고 전체가 움직이고 있다. 벽 옆에 쌓인 폭탄 더미 위로 작업등이 흔들린다.
clips.time_of_day: Interior hangar: low hard work lamps, sweat-sheened skin, heat haze, deep shadows between aircraft; muffled AA through the deck above.

[NEGATIVE]
No on-screen text, subtitles, timestamps, logos, watermarks, letterbox. No music, no narration. No modern objects. No anime/CG/plastic look, no waxy skin, no cloned faces, no extra fingers or limbs.
One aircraft never carries a bomb and a torpedo at the same time. Bombs and torpedoes are never thrown. No calm moment.

[STRUCTURE]
30s, 6 shots, hard cuts. Timings are clip time.
First frame: hangar wide: rows of B5N2s wingtip to wingtip, land bombs under their bellies; low steel ceiling, swinging work lamps, heat haze; the ORDNANCE CHIEF puts a whistle to his lips.

[SHOTS]
Shot 1 (0–5s) — WHISTLE — the hangar moves
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image6
Frame: Hangar wide. Foreground left: a B5N2 wingtip, soft. Midground centre: the ORDNANCE CHIEF with the whistle. Background: rows of B5N2s, low ceiling beams, work lamps.
Action:
- 0–1.5s: the chief blows a long blast
- 1.5–3.5s: dozens of men pour from both sides of the passage and scatter under the aircraft
- 3.5–5s: the chief swings his arm, sending crews to each aircraft — wordless shouting
Camera: 24mm, fast push-in from behind the chief.
Light: low yellow work-lamp light, sweat sheen, heat haze.
Sound: whistle, running feet, shouts, muffled guns above.
Ends on: a crew at every aircraft.

Shot 2 (5–10s) · CUT TO — CRADLE — take the weight
Refs: @image2, @image3, @image5, @image6
Frame: Low under a B5N2's belly: a bomb cart (@image5) rolls in directly beneath the land bomb (as in @image3); three crewmen.
Action:
- 5–7s: two men line the cart up exactly under the bomb
- 7–8.5s: one pumps the jack handle, raising the cradle
- 8.5–10s: the cradle meets the bomb and takes its weight; the cart's tyres squash
Camera: 35mm at floor level, slight handheld.
Light: lamp glints in the shadow under the aircraft.
Sound: jack pumping, metal contact, hard breathing.
Ends on: the cradle carrying the weight.

Shot 3 (10–14s) · CUT TO — RELEASE THE SHACKLE
Refs: @image2, @image5
Frame: Insert: the bomb shackle and a gloved hand turning a wrench; a drop of sweat falling from a brow.
Action:
- 10–12s: the wrench turns three times; a sweat drop lands on the bomb
- 12–14s: the shackle opens; the bomb drops 2cm onto the cradle with a thud
Camera: 100mm macro, locked-off.
Light: hard lamp highlights.
Sound: wrench ratchet, the thud.
Ends on: the empty shackle.

Shot 4 (14–19s) · CUT TO — OUT — the empty rack
Refs: @image2, @image5, @image4, @image6
Frame: A passage intersection: the bomb cart heading out right, a torpedo cradle (@image4) coming in from the left; behind, the B5N2 with its empty rack.
Action:
- 14–16s: four men lean into the bomb cart, pushing it right
- 16–17.5s: at the intersection it nearly collides with the torpedo cradle; both jerk to a stop
- 17.5–19s: the chief signals one to hold and waves the other through
Camera: 28mm, slow arc from high above the intersection.
Light: crossing lamp light, oil sheen on the deck plates.
Sound: rolling wheels, a sudden stop, a short whistle.
Ends on: the B5N2 showing its empty rack.

Shot 5 (19–24s) · CUT TO — NO TIME — stack them here
Refs: @image1, @image5, @image6
Frame: Hangar bulkhead: bombs begin piling beside the wall, not sent down to the magazine; fuel hoses run alongside.
Action:
- 19–21s: a crewman points toward the magazine lift; the chief shakes his head and jabs at the wall
- 21–23s: bombs are set down by the wall, one, two; a fuel hose runs right beside them
- 23–24s: the chief wipes his brow and runs to the next aircraft
Camera: 50mm, slow tracking along the bulkhead.
Light: deep shadows on the bulkhead, lamp gleam on the bombs.
FX: an ominous detail — shown plainly, not emphasised.
Sound: steel scraping the deck, breathing, guns above.
Ends on: bombs stacked beside the fuel hose.

Shot 6 (24–30s) · CUT TO — EVERYWHERE AT ONCE
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image6, @image4
Frame: A rising crane-like wide: several crews doing the same job at once; a steel beam passes through the foreground.
Action:
- 24–26s: the camera rises between beams; the whole hangar is revealed
- 26–28s: on the left bombs go out; on the right torpedoes come in
- 28–30s: the ship heels; every lamp swings at once; shadows lurch
Camera: rising crane move with a beam wipe.
Light: swinging lamps, moving shadows.
Sound: dozens of men, wheels, muffled gunfire above.
Ends on: the crush under swinging lamps.

[AUDIO]
Speak only the quoted lines, once each, in the stated language, at the stated moment. Diegetic sound only — wind, sea, engines, guns, metal, wordless voices — carried across cuts. No music, no narration.

clips.prompt:
[STYLE LOCK]
Photoreal live-action WWII epic, Battle of Midway, June 4 1942. Large-format cinema camera, spherical primes, fine film grain, soft highlight roll-off, deep atmospheric haze at distance.
Palette: steel-teal sea, milky high-key sky with towering cumulus, white coral sand, olive-drab, khaki and dark navy, warm tanned skin. Orange fire only at the instant of an explosion or a burning wing; flak is black, smoke charcoal, sea spray white. No oversaturated cyan, no game sheen.
Every frame in three layers: dark foreground occluder (sandbag, barrel, window frame, wing edge, hull rail) — subject — vast sky, sea or battle beyond. Exteriors: men small against the sky. Interiors: hard window light, haze, and the battle outside always visible or audible.
Real-time speed, no slow motion. 16:9, 1080p. Light, haze, smoke and wind stay continuous across cuts.

[TIME & PLACE]
Interior hangar: low work lamps, heat haze, sweat, swinging shadows; muffled AA above growing louder.

[IMAGES — all references, none as start/end frame]
@image1 [BG] Japanese carrier steel hangar: beams, passages, deck plates
@image2 [ASSET] B5N2 parked: wings spread, wheels down
@image3 [ASSET] B5N2 three-seat level bomber with land bomb
@image4 [ASSET] Japanese aerial torpedo on a wheeled cradle
@image5 [ASSET] Japanese ordnance carts, chocks, straps, tools
@image6 [ASSET] Japanese ordnance crew work clothes, cap, gloves

[REFERENCE LOCK]
BG images: copy layout, materials and geography only — not their camera, light or colour.
Aircraft/ship/weapon images: exact silhouette, structure, paint, markings, number of engines, barrels and funnels; never morph types.
Costume sheets: uniform and gear only, worn by living men with the CAST LOCK faces. Never show sheets, labels, mannequins or multiple views.
US insignia 1942: white star in blue circle, no red centre, no side bars. Japanese: red hinomaru.

[CAST LOCK — same faces in every shot]
ORDNANCE CHIEF — Japanese petty officer, 35. Broad flat face, shaved head glistening with sweat, thick neck, towel twisted into a headband, loud whistle on a cord.
ORDNANCE CREW — Japanese sailors, 18–25, shaved heads, white or grey work clothes darkened by sweat, cotton gloves, hachimaki or towels; every face different.
Japanese: authentic adult Japanese men of 1942 — lean, wiry, compact builds; enlisted heads shaved or near-shaved, officers short-cropped; monolid or hooded eyes, straight lower nose bridge, defined cheekbones, bronze tan, clean-shaven unless stated. Natural, dignified — never caricature, never modern idol styling.
Every other extra has a clearly different face; no clones.

[DIRECTION & PHYSICS]
American flight paths, ship headings, muzzles and profiles read RIGHT-TO-LEFT; Japanese read LEFT-TO-RIGHT — by camera placement, never by mirroring.
Propellers are blurred discs; aircraft keep exact shape; torpedoes fall nose-slightly-down, splash, then run straight leaving a bubble wake; bombs keep forward momentum; recoil, casings, spray and debris obey gravity. A destroyed aircraft never reappears. The camera never passes through glass, walls or hulls.

[NEGATIVE]
No on-screen text, subtitles, timestamps, logos, watermarks, letterbox. No music, no narration. No modern objects. No anime/CG/plastic look, no waxy skin, no cloned faces, no extra fingers or limbs.
One aircraft never carries a bomb and a torpedo at the same time. Torpedoes are never thrown or dropped on the deck.

[STRUCTURE]
26s, 5 shots, hard cuts. Timings are clip time.
First frame: hangar floor level: four men push a cradle carrying a long torpedo in from frame left; lamp light slides along its silver body.

[SHOTS]
Shot 1 (0–5s) — TORPEDO IN
Refs: @image4, @image1, @image6
Frame: Floor level. Foreground: a deck-plate seam. Midground: the torpedo cradle (@image4) and four men pushing. Background: a B5N2's empty rack.
Action:
- 0–2s: four men push the cradle; lamp light slides along the torpedo
- 2–3.5s: the front wheel catches on the plate seam; the cradle jerks
- 3.5–5s: they heave together; the wheel jumps the seam; the torpedo bounces once on its cradle; hands steady it at once
Camera: 24mm at floor level, tracking backward with the cradle.
Light: highlights on the torpedo body, sweat.
Sound: wheels, a thud, breathing, a wordless heave-call.
Ends on: the torpedo arriving under the empty rack.

Shot 2 (5–10s) · CUT TO — ALIGN
Refs: @image2, @image4, @image5, @image6
Frame: Under the B5N2's belly: one man guides the torpedo nose, another the tail fins.
Action:
- 5–7s: the jack lifts the torpedo slowly
- 7–9s: a tail fin nearly touches the fuselage; the rear man twists it true with his palm
- 9–10s: the torpedo stops just below the rack
Camera: 35mm low under the fuselage, a very slow tilt up with the lift.
Light: aircraft shadow, silver torpedo.
Sound: jack, metal brushing metal.
Ends on: the torpedo just under the rack.

Shot 3 (10–14s) · CUT TO — LOCK
Refs: @image5, @image2, @image6
Frame: Insert: the shackle closes, a strap is cinched; the chief's palm slaps the torpedo.
Action:
- 10–11.5s: the shackle snaps shut
- 11.5–13s: a strap is pulled tight twice
- 13–14s: the chief's palm slaps the torpedo
Camera: 100mm macro, locked-off.
Light: hard lamp highlights.
Sound: snap, strap, slap.
Ends on: the torpedo secured.

Shot 4 (14–19s) · CUT TO — THE SHIP LURCHES
Refs: @image1, @image6, @image5
Frame: Hangar medium-wide: a near miss above; lamps swing; an empty cart rolls.
Action:
- 14–15.5s: a dull blast; the hangar tilts; dust falls from the ceiling
- 15.5–17.5s: an empty cart rolls by itself; two men throw their bodies against it
- 17.5–19s: everyone looks up once, then goes straight back to work
Camera: 28mm handheld, shaken.
Light: swinging light, streams of dust.
Sound: the blast, groaning metal, rolling wheels, guns above.
Ends on: hands back at work.

Shot 5 (19–26s) · CUT TO — NOT DONE YET
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image3, @image6
Frame: Long diagonal wide: B5N2s in front now with torpedoes, those behind still with bombs; the bomb pile by the wall; sweat-soaked men.
Action:
- 19–21.5s: the camera glides along the row past converted and unconverted aircraft
- 21.5–24s: the chief wipes his sweat and looks up; the gunfire above grows heavier
- 24–26s: a swinging work lamp crosses the lens in a white flare — cut
Camera: 35mm slow lateral tracking along the row, ending on a lamp flare.
Light: yellow lamps, deep shadows, sweat.
Sound: work noise, AA overhead growing louder.
Ends on: the lamp flare.

[AUDIO]
Speak only the quoted lines, once each, in the stated language, at the stated moment. Diegetic sound only — wind, sea, engines, guns, metal, wordless voices — carried across cuts. No music, no narration.

clips.prompt:
[STYLE LOCK]
Photoreal live-action WWII epic, Battle of Midway, June 4 1942. Large-format cinema camera, spherical primes, fine film grain, soft highlight roll-off, deep atmospheric haze at distance.
Palette: steel-teal sea, milky high-key sky with towering cumulus, white coral sand, olive-drab, khaki and dark navy, warm tanned skin. Orange fire only at the instant of an explosion or a burning wing; flak is black, smoke charcoal, sea spray white. No oversaturated cyan, no game sheen.
Every frame in three layers: dark foreground occluder (sandbag, barrel, window frame, wing edge, hull rail) — subject — vast sky, sea or battle beyond. Exteriors: men small against the sky. Interiors: hard window light, haze, and the battle outside always visible or audible.
Real-time speed, no slow motion. 16:9, 1080p. Light, haze, smoke and wind stay continuous across cuts.

[TIME & PLACE]
Late morning: high sun, sea glare, flak and white shell splashes over a low, slow line of aircraft.

[IMAGES — all references, none as start/end frame]
@image1 [BG] open Pacific surface, far horizon, broken cumulus
@image2 [ASSET] Kagero-class destroyer: hull, two funnels, gun mounts
@image3 [ASSET] carrier Akagi: hull, hinomaru on bow, island on PORT side, downward-curved funnel on STARBOARD side
@image4 [ASSET] TBD-1 Devastator: long tandem canopy, blue-grey, corrugated wings, main wheels half-protruding when retracted
@image5 [ASSET] Japanese twin 25mm AA mount: two parallel barrels, carriage, sights
@image6 [ASSET] Japanese AA crew uniform, helmet, magazine gear
@image7 [ASSET] US Mark 13 aerial torpedo: long body, nose, tail, mount

[REFERENCE LOCK]
BG images: copy layout, materials and geography only — not their camera, light or colour.
Aircraft/ship/weapon images: exact silhouette, structure, paint, markings, number of engines, barrels and funnels; never morph types.
Costume sheets: uniform and gear only, worn by living men with the CAST LOCK faces. Never show sheets, labels, mannequins or multiple views.
US insignia 1942: white star in blue circle, no red centre, no side bars. Japanese: red hinomaru.

[CAST LOCK — same faces in every shot]
AKAGI LOOKOUT — Japanese petty officer, 30. Square weathered face, deep vertical frown line between the brows, near-shaved head under a white cap cover, chin strap, large pedestal binoculars.
JAPANESE AA GUNNER — Japanese sailor, 21. Thin face, sharp jaw, shaved head under a steel helmet with chin strap, gritted teeth, white undershirt, sweat; sits in the pointer seat of a twin 25mm mount.
JAPANESE AA LOADER — Japanese sailor, 19. Round boyish face, near-shaved head, wide-set eyes, flushed cheeks, white towel around his neck, slams 15-round box magazines onto the gun.
Americans: varied European-American ancestry (Irish, Italian, German, Polish), varied hair colour, deeper-set eyes, higher nose bridges, forearm hair, sunburnt red-pink skin, stubble, sweat. Real 1942 faces — no movie-star polish.
Japanese: authentic adult Japanese men of 1942 — lean, wiry, compact builds; enlisted heads shaved or near-shaved, officers short-cropped; monolid or hooded eyes, straight lower nose bridge, defined cheekbones, bronze tan, clean-shaven unless stated. Natural, dignified — never caricature, never modern idol styling.
Every other extra has a clearly different face; no clones.

[DIRECTION & PHYSICS]
American flight paths, ship headings, muzzles and profiles read RIGHT-TO-LEFT; Japanese read LEFT-TO-RIGHT — by camera placement, never by mirroring.
Propellers are blurred discs; aircraft keep exact shape; torpedoes fall nose-slightly-down, splash, then run straight leaving a bubble wake; bombs keep forward momentum; recoil, casings, spray and debris obey gravity. A destroyed aircraft never reappears. The camera never passes through glass, walls or hulls.

[NEGATIVE]
No on-screen text, subtitles, timestamps, logos, watermarks, letterbox. No music, no narration. No modern objects. No anime/CG/plastic look, no waxy skin, no cloned faces, no extra fingers or limbs.
The TBDs fly very low (10–20 m) and close to the ships, not far away. Japanese guns are fired by visible men. Only one TBD (not A or B) crashes here.

[STRUCTURE]
26s, 5 shots, hard cuts. Timings are clip time.
First frame: a second destroyer steams left-to-right, guns trained right; beyond her bow, low specks on the horizon.

[SHOTS]
Shot 1 (0–5s) — ANOTHER DESTROYER
Refs: @image1, @image2
Frame: Low oblique over the water. Left two-thirds: a destroyer (@image2) running left-to-right, bow spray. Right horizon: low specks.
Action:
- 0–2.5s: the destroyer crosses frame; her guns swing right
- 2.5–5s: the specks on the horizon grow slowly, hugging the sea
Camera: 2 metres above the water, slow tracking with the destroyer.
Light: glittering sea, grey hull.
Sound: bow wave, distant many-engine drone, a far explosion.
Ends on: the specks on the horizon.

Shot 2 (5–10s) · CUT TO — LOOKOUT POV — torpedo bombers
Refs: @image1, @image4, @image2
Frame: The AKAGI LOOKOUT's binocular POV, twin-circle vignette: beyond the destroyers, a long line of TBDs 10–20 metres above the sea.
Action:
- 5–7s: the binoculars sweep and stop on the low line
- 7–10s: focus pulls in: about fifteen TBDs crawling toward them, glued to the sea
Camera: binocular POV, hand tremor.
Light: haze, low contrast.
Sound: wind, the lookout's breath.
Ends on: the low line spanning the frame.

Shot 3 (10–15s) · CUT TO — LOW AND SLOW — the Devastators
Refs: @image1, @image4, @image7, @image2
Frame: Side view over the sea. Foreground: the nearest TBD (@image4), torpedo (@image7) under its belly. Background: more TBDs, destroyers far off.
Action:
- 10–12.5s: the TBDs crawl right-to-left 15 metres above the sea; propwash ruffles the surface
- 12.5–15s: the first shell columns erupt ahead of them
Camera: aerial side tracking close to the water.
Light: glittering sea, blue-grey aircraft.
Sound: slow radial engines, wind, splashes.
Ends on: the line flying into the columns.

Shot 4 (15–20s) · CUT TO — THEY SHOOT — Japanese gunners
Refs: @image5, @image6, @image2
Frame: On the destroyer's mount: the AA GUNNER cranks the barrels low; the AA LOADER holds a magazine; the low TBD line behind.
Action:
- 15–17s: the gunner depresses the barrels almost level
- 17–19s: he fires; tracers stream out flat and low; brass pours
- 19–20s: the loader slams a magazine home
Camera: 40mm from behind the mount, over the barrels.
Light: muzzle flash, smoke.
Sound: twin bursts, brass.
Ends on: firing continuing.

Shot 5 (20–26s) · CUT TO — FIRST LOSS
Refs: @image1, @image4
Frame: Medium on the TBD line amid flak and shell splashes.
Action:
- 20–22s: flak bursts among the line; cannon splashes stitch the water
- 22–24s: one TBD (neither A nor B) has its wing burst into fire; its nose drops
- 24–26s: it slams into the sea in a column of water; the rest hold their line and fly past
Camera: aerial side tracking, a brief hold on the impact.
Light: black smoke, white water, orange flame.
Sound: blast, water impact, engines continuing.
Ends on: the line passing the column.

[AUDIO]
Speak only the quoted lines, once each, in the stated language, at the stated moment. Diegetic sound only — wind, sea, engines, guns, metal, wordless voices — carried across cuts. No music, no narration.

clips.prompt:
[STYLE LOCK]
Photoreal live-action WWII epic, Battle of Midway, June 4 1942. Large-format cinema camera, spherical primes, fine film grain, soft highlight roll-off, deep atmospheric haze at distance.
Palette: steel-teal sea, milky high-key sky with towering cumulus, white coral sand, olive-drab, khaki and dark navy, warm tanned skin. Orange fire only at the instant of an explosion or a burning wing; flak is black, smoke charcoal, sea spray white. No oversaturated cyan, no game sheen.
Every frame in three layers: dark foreground occluder (sandbag, barrel, window frame, wing edge, hull rail) — subject — vast sky, sea or battle beyond. Exteriors: men small against the sky. Interiors: hard window light, haze, and the battle outside always visible or audible.
Real-time speed, no slow motion. 16:9, 1080p. Light, haze, smoke and wind stay continuous across cuts.

[TIME & PLACE]
Late morning: high sun overhead (Zeros dive out of it), glare, flak.

[IMAGES — all references, none as start/end frame]
@image1 [BG] open Pacific surface, far horizon, broken cumulus
@image2 [ASSET] TBD-1 Devastator: long tandem canopy, blue-grey, corrugated wings, main wheels half-protruding when retracted
@image3 [ASSET] US Navy aircrew flight suit, helmet, yellow life vest
@image4 [ASSET] TBD front cockpit: narrow, gauges, canopy rails
@image5 [ASSET] A6M2 Zero, grey-green, red hinomaru, wheels retracted, no drop tank
@image6 [ASSET] Kagero-class destroyer: hull, two funnels, gun mounts
@image7 [ASSET] US Mark 13 aerial torpedo: long body, nose, tail, mount
@image8 [ASSET] US flexible rear machine gun: receiver, barrel, ammo feed, ring mount

[REFERENCE LOCK]
BG images: copy layout, materials and geography only — not their camera, light or colour.
Aircraft/ship/weapon images: exact silhouette, structure, paint, markings, number of engines, barrels and funnels; never morph types.
Costume sheets: uniform and gear only, worn by living men with the CAST LOCK faces. Never show sheets, labels, mannequins or multiple views.
US insignia 1942: white star in blue circle, no red centre, no side bars. Japanese: red hinomaru.

[CAST LOCK — same faces in every shot]
TBD PILOT B — American Navy, 23. Long narrow face, dark-brown wavy hair, hooded brown eyes, long straight nose, olive tan, khaki flight suit, yellow life vest.
REAR GUNNER — American Navy, 19. Skinny, prominent ears, short mousy-brown hair, boyish chin, sunburnt nose, goggles on his helmet.
ZERO PILOT — Japanese naval aviator, 24. Rounder face, thick straight eyebrows, single-lid eyes, small pale scar on the left side of the chin, clean-shaven, leather helmet and goggles.
Americans: varied European-American ancestry (Irish, Italian, German, Polish), varied hair colour, deeper-set eyes, higher nose bridges, forearm hair, sunburnt red-pink skin, stubble, sweat. Real 1942 faces — no movie-star polish.
Japanese: authentic adult Japanese men of 1942 — lean, wiry, compact builds; enlisted heads shaved or near-shaved, officers short-cropped; monolid or hooded eyes, straight lower nose bridge, defined cheekbones, bronze tan, clean-shaven unless stated. Natural, dignified — never caricature, never modern idol styling.
Every other extra has a clearly different face; no clones.

[DIRECTION & PHYSICS]
American flight paths, ship headings, muzzles and profiles read RIGHT-TO-LEFT; Japanese read LEFT-TO-RIGHT — by camera placement, never by mirroring.
Propellers are blurred discs; aircraft keep exact shape; torpedoes fall nose-slightly-down, splash, then run straight leaving a bubble wake; bombs keep forward momentum; recoil, casings, spray and debris obey gravity. A destroyed aircraft never reappears. The camera never passes through glass, walls or hulls.

[NEGATIVE]
No on-screen text, subtitles, timestamps, logos, watermarks, letterbox. No music, no narration. No modern objects. No anime/CG/plastic look, no waxy skin, no cloned faces, no extra fingers or limbs.
B is undamaged at the start of this clip and still carries its torpedo. TBD A does not reappear.

[STRUCTURE]
26s, 6 shots, hard cuts. Timings are clip time.
First frame: foam left by A on the sea; from the right, an undamaged TBD B enters with one torpedo.

[SHOTS]
Shot 1 (0–5s) — B ENTERS
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image7
Frame: Sea level. Foreground: A's foam and debris. TBD B enters from the right — clean wings, torpedo under its belly.
Action:
- 0–2s: B's shadow crosses the foam first
- 2–5s: B passes behind the foam right-to-left, more distant squadron-mates following
Camera: fixed above the water, then pan with B.
Light: glittering water, shadow.
Sound: engine Doppler, lapping water.
Ends on: B heading left.

Shot 2 (5–10s) · CUT TO — INCOMING FIRE — the canopy
Refs: @image4, @image3, @image6
Frame: Inside B's cockpit: tracers and shells streak past beyond the canopy rails; PILOT B.
Action:
- 5–7s: tracer lines flash past outside the canopy
- 7–8.5s: a round punches through the glass, leaving a hole and cracks; B flinches
- 8.5–10s: a near-miss flash floods the cockpit white
Camera: 35mm inside the cockpit at shoulder height, vibration.
Light: white flash, canopy-frame shadows.
Sound: glass cracking, rounds hissing past, blasts.
Ends on: the white flash clearing.

Shot 3 (10–14s) · CUT TO — REAR SEAT — eyes up
Refs: @image3, @image8, @image2
Frame: Rear seat: the REAR GUNNER beside the flexible gun (@image8) looks up.
Action:
- 10–12s: the gunner pulls his goggles down and scans the sky
- 12–14s: he spots two dots in the sun and pounds the pilot's seat back with his fist
Camera: 50mm outside the rear seat.
Light: sun flare overhead.
Sound: wind, the fist thumps.
Ends on: the gunner pointing up.

Shot 4 (14–17s) · CUT TO — THE CALL
Refs: @image3, @image4
Frame: PILOT B close-up, right third, looking up-left.
Action:
- 14–15s: B looks up-left toward the new engine sound
- 15–17s: he shouts; too low to evade, he grips the stick
Dialogue (TBD PILOT B, English, shouted, urgent) at 15–17s: "Zero incoming!"
Camera: 85mm close-up.
Light: sunlight through the canopy.
Sound: the shout, a high engine closing.
Ends on: the gripped stick.

Shot 5 (17–22s) · CUT TO — OUT OF THE SUN
Refs: @image5, @image1
Frame: Sky beside the sun: two Zeros (@image5) roll over and dive; far below, the low TBDs and the sea.
Action:
- 17–19s: the first Zero rolls over inside the sun flare
- 19–22s: both dive in turn; small silhouettes grow fast, passing from bright sky to dark sea behind them
Camera: aerial, following the dive from behind.
Light: sun flare, silhouettes.
Sound: a high-pitched engine diving.
Ends on: the Zeros growing.

Shot 6 (22–26s) · CUT TO — GUN UP
Refs: @image8, @image3, @image2
Frame: Close on the REAR GUNNER: charging handle, ammunition belt.
Action:
- 22–24s: he yanks the charging handle; the belt jumps
- 24–26s: he swings the gun up at the diving Zeros
Camera: 50mm handheld, tilting up along the barrel.
Light: backlight, sweat.
Sound: the cocking clack, wind.
Ends on: the muzzle aimed at the sky.

[AUDIO]
Speak only the quoted lines, once each, in the stated language, at the stated moment. Diegetic sound only — wind, sea, engines, guns, metal, wordless voices — carried across cuts. No music, no narration.

clips.prompt:
[STYLE LOCK]
Photoreal live-action WWII epic, Battle of Midway, June 4 1942. Large-format cinema camera, spherical primes, fine film grain, soft highlight roll-off, deep atmospheric haze at distance.
Palette: steel-teal sea, milky high-key sky with towering cumulus, white coral sand, olive-drab, khaki and dark navy, warm tanned skin. Orange fire only at the instant of an explosion or a burning wing; flak is black, smoke charcoal, sea spray white. No oversaturated cyan, no game sheen.
Every frame in three layers: dark foreground occluder (sandbag, barrel, window frame, wing edge, hull rail) — subject — vast sky, sea or battle beyond. Exteriors: men small against the sky. Interiors: hard window light, haze, and the battle outside always visible or audible.
Real-time speed, no slow motion. 16:9, 1080p. Light, haze, smoke and wind stay continuous across cuts.

[TIME & PLACE]
Late morning: high sun, glare, flak; the final shot under the surface with blue light shafts.

[IMAGES — all references, none as start/end frame]
@image1 [BG] open Pacific surface, far horizon, broken cumulus
@image2 [ASSET] TBD-1 Devastator: long tandem canopy, blue-grey, corrugated wings, main wheels half-protruding when retracted
@image3 [ASSET] US Navy aircrew flight suit, helmet, yellow life vest
@image4 [ASSET] TBD front cockpit: narrow, gauges, canopy rails
@image5 [ASSET] US flexible rear machine gun: receiver, barrel, ammo feed, ring mount
@image6 [ASSET] A6M2 Zero, grey-green, red hinomaru, wheels retracted, no drop tank
@image7 [ASSET] Japanese naval aviator flight suit, leather helmet, goggles
@image8 [ASSET] US Mark 13 aerial torpedo: long body, nose, tail, mount
@image9 [ASSET] carrier Akagi: hull, hinomaru on bow, island on PORT side, downward-curved funnel on STARBOARD side

[REFERENCE LOCK]
BG images: copy layout, materials and geography only — not their camera, light or colour.
Aircraft/ship/weapon images: exact silhouette, structure, paint, markings, number of engines, barrels and funnels; never morph types.
Costume sheets: uniform and gear only, worn by living men with the CAST LOCK faces. Never show sheets, labels, mannequins or multiple views.
US insignia 1942: white star in blue circle, no red centre, no side bars. Japanese: red hinomaru.

[CAST LOCK — same faces in every shot]
TBD PILOT B — American Navy, 23. Long narrow face, dark-brown wavy hair, hooded brown eyes, long straight nose, olive tan, khaki flight suit, yellow life vest.
REAR GUNNER — American Navy, 19. Skinny, prominent ears, short mousy-brown hair, boyish chin, sunburnt nose, goggles on his helmet.
ZERO PILOT — Japanese naval aviator, 24. Rounder face, thick straight eyebrows, single-lid eyes, small pale scar on the left side of the chin, clean-shaven, leather helmet and goggles.
Americans: varied European-American ancestry (Irish, Italian, German, Polish), varied hair colour, deeper-set eyes, higher nose bridges, forearm hair, sunburnt red-pink skin, stubble, sweat. Real 1942 faces — no movie-star polish.
Japanese: authentic adult Japanese men of 1942 — lean, wiry, compact builds; enlisted heads shaved or near-shaved, officers short-cropped; monolid or hooded eyes, straight lower nose bridge, defined cheekbones, bronze tan, clean-shaven unless stated. Natural, dignified — never caricature, never modern idol styling.
Every other extra has a clearly different face; no clones.

[DIRECTION & PHYSICS]
American flight paths, ship headings, muzzles and profiles read RIGHT-TO-LEFT; Japanese read LEFT-TO-RIGHT — by camera placement, never by mirroring.
Propellers are blurred discs; aircraft keep exact shape; torpedoes fall nose-slightly-down, splash, then run straight leaving a bubble wake; bombs keep forward momentum; recoil, casings, spray and debris obey gravity. A destroyed aircraft never reappears. The camera never passes through glass, walls or hulls.

[NEGATIVE]
No on-screen text, subtitles, timestamps, logos, watermarks, letterbox. No music, no narration. No modern objects. No anime/CG/plastic look, no waxy skin, no cloned faces, no extra fingers or limbs.
B drops exactly one torpedo before it is hit; its rack stays empty. No Japanese victory smiles or cheering. No hit on the carrier.

[STRUCTURE]
30s, 7 shots, hard cuts. Timings are clip time.
First frame: low wide over the sea: a smoking TBD drops its torpedo while sinking lower; ahead of it, B pulls its release.

[SHOTS]
Shot 1 (0–5s) — DROPPING WHILE DYING
Refs: @image1, @image2, @image8, @image9
Frame: Low wide over the sea. Foreground: B with its torpedo. Midground: another TBD trailing smoke. Background: Akagi.
Action:
- 0–2s: the smoking TBD drops its torpedo even as it sinks lower; the torpedo splashes
- 2–3.5s: B's torpedo drops from its belly and enters the water shallow
- 3.5–5s: B flies on, rack empty; the smoking TBD touches the sea
Camera: side tracking 2 metres above the water.
Light: glittering sea, black smoke, white splashes.
Sound: engines, entry splashes, an impact.
Ends on: B with an empty rack.

Shot 2 (5–9s) · CUT TO — THE DIVE
Refs: @image6, @image2, @image1
Frame: Top to bottom: three Zeros diving in line onto the TBDs over the sea.
Action:
- 5–7s: the Zeros dive one after another
- 7–9s: wing guns flash; impact splashes stitch the sea
Camera: aerial, tracking from above and behind the Zeros.
Light: backlight, silhouettes.
Sound: diving whine, cannon.
Ends on: the Zeros falling on the line.

Shot 3 (9–12s) · CUT TO — ZERO PILOT
Refs: @image7, @image6
Frame: Zero cockpit: the ZERO PILOT in right profile; the sea streaming past outside.
Action:
- 9–10s: the pilot presses his eye to the sight
- 10–12s: he fires a short burst; eye and sight fixed, only the sea moves
Acting: no triumph — just work.
Camera: 85mm side profile, vibration.
Light: canopy-frame shadows, muzzle flash.
Sound: a short cannon burst.
Ends on: an emotionless eye.

Shot 4 (12–16s) · CUT TO — B IS HIT — left wing root
Refs: @image2, @image6, @image1
Frame: Crossing wide: the Zero above going left-to-right, B below going right-to-left.
Action:
- 12–14s: they cross; rounds punch into B's port wing root, metal flying
- 14–16s: the wing sags and catches fire; the Zero pulls away past B's tail without colliding
Camera: aerial side tracking, a short shake at the cross.
Light: orange flame, black smoke.
Sound: rounds punching metal, flame.
Ends on: the burning port wing.

Shot 5 (16–20s) · CUT TO — RETURN FIRE
Refs: @image5, @image3, @image6
Frame: Close on the REAR GUNNER; the Zero receding beyond the muzzle.
Action:
- 16–18s: he fires a short burst; tracers reach for the Zero but the shaking airframe throws them wide
- 18–20s: he braces with his shoulder and fires again; casings whip away in the wind
Camera: 50mm handheld, heavy shake.
Light: muzzle flash, smoke.
Sound: machine-gun bursts, wind.
Ends on: the Zero escaping.

Shot 6 (20–25s) · CUT TO — LAST FIGHT — the pilot
Refs: @image3, @image4, @image1
Frame: PILOT B, front three-quarter; the tilted horizon beyond the canopy.
Action:
- 20–22s: B hauls the stick to bring the tilted horizon back
- 22–23.5s: the horizon returns for a moment, then the sea rises again
- 23.5–25s: mouth shut, he holds on to the end
Camera: 50mm outside the canopy front, vibration.
Light: firelight on his face, smoke.
Sound: engine coughing, fire, wind.
Ends on: the sea filling the canopy.

Shot 7 (25–30s) · CUT TO — THE SEA TAKES HIM
Refs: @image2, @image1
Frame: Sea level, then under the surface: B's port wingtip touches the water.
Action:
- 25–27s: the port wing catches the water; the fuselage is dragged down left under a low wall of water
- 27–28s: the fire goes out; only foam and small debris remain
- 28–30s: under the surface: B sinks slowly through bubbles and blue light shafts; above, Japanese engines fade away
Camera: a descending move from 1 metre above the water to just under the surface.
Light: white water to blue underwater light shafts.
FX: B never resurfaces.
Sound: impact, water crashing, muffled underwater silence, fading engines.
Ends on: the aircraft sinking into the light shafts.

[AUDIO]
Speak only the quoted lines, once each, in the stated language, at the stated moment. Diegetic sound only — wind, sea, engines, guns, metal, wordless voices — carried across cuts. No music, no narration.

screenplay_coverage: 미드웨이 기지에서 일본이 올 것을 알고 준비
레이더 탐지·전화 보고 → 해 뜨는 활주로를 걸어서 포좌로, 느긋한 포 준비.
레이더에 잡힌 걸 발견하고 일본군이 온다고 알림
레이더병이 대편대 방위·거리 보고.
관측소에서 망원경으로 보고 “Japanese!”
쌍안경 비네트 속 어렴풋한 1차 선발대 → 관측병 외침 → 담배가 떨어지는 정적.
공습이라 외치는 사람들 빼고 다급하게 포 진지로 · 이때 전투기는 상공에 없음
말한 사람 외 전원이 6문 포좌로 질주. 포신들이 빈 하늘을 겨눈다.
미드웨이 섬 미국 선발대 출격
F4F·B-26 연속 이륙 → 편대 형성 → 빈 격납고.
일본 비행기들 떼로 오고 대공포, 미드웨이 여기저기 폭격
구름 사이 백여 대 → 돌격 명령 → 일제 사격 → 급강하 → 빈 격납고 폭발.
미드웨이에 미군 전투기 복귀 장면 필요 없음
넣지 않음. 출격한 공격대가 곧바로 일본 함대를 찾는다.
출격한 뇌격기들이 일본 함대를 찾아 공격 · “일본 함대 발견! 발사!”
구름 아래 기동부대 발견 “Japanese fleet ahead!” → 투하 순간 “Release!”(대본 한 줄을 발견·투하 두 지점으로 나눔).
선박 근처에서 어뢰 발사하지만 거의 맞고 떨어진다 · 저고도로 선박 옆에서 떨어뜨려야
B-26이 갑판 높이보다 낮게 선체 옆을 지나고, 함선 옆에서 투하. 두 대 추락.
일본 선박의 공격을 많이 받는다
구축함·아카기 포좌의 사수·급탄수가 실제로 쏘고 탄창을 간다. 링 조준기 POV.
선실 내부 소리 빼고 바로 방향 트는 항모 · 옆으로 떨어지는 어뢰들 · 전투기들도
아카기 급선회, 선체 옆·함미 뒤로 흐르는 어뢰, 위로 제로센.
구축함 외경: 전투기 떨어지는 장면 빼고 어뢰가 옆으로 떨어지는 장면만
추락기 없이 어뢰만 선체 옆에 입수.
나구모 명령 장면 · 밖은 아수라장(미국 공격기, 일본 함대 대포)
창 너머 B-26 통과·대공 연기·근탄 물기둥·유리 떨림이 모든 샷에. 육상 폭탄 교체 명령.
미국 군함들 보이는 부감
엔터프라이즈와 호위함 부감.
부하2 달려와 “적의 군함 10척” · 나구모 난감·불안(영상과 다르게) · 밖이 너무 조용
용지를 들고 달려오는 참모 → 과장된 당황 → 장갑을 벗고 갈등. 창밖 사격 지속.
미군 항모에서 여러 대가 떠서 일본 치러 가는 느낌 · 일본-미국-일본
항모와 공중의 여러 기체를 한 화면에, 깃발 발진, TBD 이륙, 편대가 수평선으로.
안절부절하던 나구모 · 밖이 너무 조용
서성임, 근탄 진동, 두 장의 종이. 창밖 전투 지속.
결단: 어뢰와 철갑폭탄으로 재무장 · 부하2의 우려 · “전투기들이 있잖아!”
명령서를 밀어내고 보고서를 내리침 → 우려 → 창밖 제로센을 가리킴.
보고 장면 빼고 폭탄 교체만 · 좀 더 바쁘게 조금 길게
격납고 2클립(56초): 호루라기, 받침, 걸쇠, 반출, 벽 옆 적재, 어뢰 반입·장착, 흔들리는 배.
다른 구축함 보이고 미국 뇌격기들 날아온다
두 번째 구축함 → 견시원 쌍안경 → 해면 위 TBD 대열.
일본군 방어 · 배 안에서 대공포 쏘는 일본군이 없다 → 여기서도 공격받아야
구축함 사수가 포신을 수평까지 낮춰 사격. 한 대 추락.
뇌격기 어뢰 떨어뜨리는 장면(참고 영상)
A 조종석 → 투하 레버 → 분리·입수·빈 거치대 → 피탄 → 추락.
조종간으로 포탄 날아오는 장면 · “Zero incoming!”
B 캐노피 밖 예광탄·관통 → 후방 사수 발견 → 외침.
떨어지면서 어뢰 떨어뜨리고, 위에서 제로센 하강 공격, 뇌격기들 추락
가라앉으며 투하 → 제로센 하강 → 조종사 사격 → B 피탄 → 응사 → 추락·침몰.
excluded_from_plan: 여러 사람이 따로 공습을 외치는 군중 장면.
항모 회피에 앞선 일본 선실 내부 소음 장면(대본).
구축함 외경에 겹치던 미군기 추락(대본). 해당 위치는 어뢰 입수만.
미 항모에서 한 기체씩 준비하는 반복 인서트(대본). 출발 항모와 여러 기체가 함께 보이는 전경으로.
재무장 명령 직후 같은 명령을 다시 보고하는 장면(대본).
adaptation_notes: 대본의 “구축함 선실의 나구모”는 아카기 함교로 바로잡았다. 구축함은 외경·대공 사격에 사용한다.
대본의 항공기용 “육상 포탄”은 일본어 명령에서 “육상 폭탄(陸用爆弾)”으로 표현한다.
대본의 “일본 함대 발견! 발사!” 한 줄을 발견(C02 “Japanese fleet ahead!”)과 투하(C04 “Release!”) 두 지점으로 나눴다. 그 사이에 저공 접근이 들어가기 때문이다.
미드웨이 공격대는 기존 에셋 B-26(어뢰 장착)으로 보여준다. 한 대가 아카기 갑판 위를 스치고, 불붙은 한 대가 함교 옆을 스쳐 추락하는 것은 실제 기록에 가까운 각색이다.
C09의 출발 항모는 기존 에셋인 엔터프라이즈 CV-6. C13 이후 호넷 제8뇌격대는 별도 공격 대열이며 CV-6를 호넷으로 표기하지 않는다.
C11의 ‘탄약고로 돌려보낼 시간이 없어 벽 옆에 쌓는 폭탄’은 실제 기록에 근거한 디테일이다. 화면에서 강조하지 않고 보여만 준다.
대사와 인물 반응은 사용자의 대본을 따른 극화다. 실제 인물의 발언 기록을 옮겼다는 뜻이 아니다.
레이더 탐지 05:53, 첫 대편대 약 108대, 미드웨이 신천옹 등은 실제 기록에 맞춘 디테일이다.
영화 프레임·첨부 영상은 구도·속도·전경 가림·크기 대비 참고용. 기체·사건·자막을 복제하지 않는다.
